# The Tan Running Route Guide

Use Melbourne’s 3.827 km circuit for repeatable aerobic runs and hill-effort practice. Plan the distance before you start, then let Anderson Street set the effort.

Online sources checked 13 October 2026 · [Editorial policy](https://marathonpacekm.com/editorial-policy/)

## Quick facts

| Fact | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Distance | 3.827 km official event lap |
| Surface | Fine gravel; sealed Anderson Street section |
| Terrain | Anderson Street climb: about 30 m over 300 m |
| Fountains | Council documents nearby Alexandra Gardens fountains |
| Start / finish | Pillars of Wisdom for the official clockwise lap |
| Lighting | Organiser reports 5 am–midnight |

Sources: [Course distance and direction](https://runthetan.net/the-course/) · [Council terrain guide](https://whatson.melbourne.vic.gov.au/article/the-best-outdoor-exercise-parks-in-melbourne) · [Organiser lighting information](https://runthetan.net/about-us/) · [Nearby amenities](https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/stolen-generations-marker/proposed-locations).

## The route and what changes the effort

[Run the Tan’s official lap](https://runthetan.net/the-course/) starts at the Pillars of Wisdom and covers 3.827 km clockwise around the Royal Botanic Gardens and Kings Domain. Head along Alexandra Avenue, turn up Anderson Street, then follow the perimeter towards Birdwood Avenue and back to Alexandra Avenue. Keep the gardens on your right for this published circuit.

The main surface is fine gravel, with a sealed section on Anderson Street. The [City of Melbourne describes the hill](https://whatson.melbourne.vic.gov.au/article/things-to-do-at-royal-botanic-gardens-melbourne) as rising about 30 m over 300 m. That figure describes the climb, rather than the elevation gain of the whole circuit. Ease your pace uphill and judge the effort before trying to recover seconds on the descent.

## Plan 10 km, 21.1 km or 30 km

The table uses 3.827 km per official lap. The added distances are arithmetic remainders, not surveyed extensions or marked finish points. After your full laps, continue on the circuit for the remaining distance you have planned. If you finish part-way around, allow separately for getting back to your starting point.

Calculated session distances using the published lap length

| Session target | Full laps | Then add |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 km | 2 = 7.654 km | 2.346 km |
| 21.1 km | 5 = 19.135 km | 1.965 km |
| 30 km | 7 = 26.789 km | 3.211 km |

If returning to your start matters more than a round number, three laps total 11.481 km, six total 22.962 km and eight total 30.616 km. Choose that distance deliberately; an extra whole lap is a substantial addition to an already planned long run. The 21.1 km option is a rounded training target, rather than a certified half-marathon course.

GPS readings can differ from the published lap distance. Use the arithmetic to plan, then your watch or markers to manage a partial lap. Leave room for other users at the finish.

## Best uses in marathon training

### Easy and recovery runs

Decide after each lap whether to finish or continue. Keep the hill easy enough that the run serves its planned purpose; defend the recovery effort rather than a fixed kilometre pace.

### Long runs and fuel practice

Repeated laps return you to the same starting area for an arranged bottle handover. Plan any stop as part of the session. For continuous fuel practice, carry your supplies. Record elapsed time and stops so you can interpret later laps at a comparable effort.

### Tempo and race-specific blocks

Practise allowing pace to change while controlling effort on the hill. That skill transfers to a rolling marathon course. For a flatter race, choose a measured track or flatter route when the session’s purpose is holding a narrow pace range.

## Crowding, interruptions and practical planning

The council’s [run-club listing schedules Saturday sessions from 8–10 am](https://whatson.melbourne.vic.gov.au/things-to-do/run-the-tan-run-club). Run the Tan also documents established clubs and annual events here. That supports its place in a Melbourne training shortlist and gives you a concrete period to consider when arranging a faster session.

Give groups and walkers room, and slow down before passing where visibility is limited. Follow current signs at path junctions and any works diversions. If an interruption breaks a tempo block, record it and continue by effort rather than accelerating abruptly to make the watch average match a target.

## Water, toilets, lighting and transport

The organiser lists nearby toilets along Alexandra Avenue, at the Sidney Myer Music Bowl and inside the gardens. The [council’s Alexandra Gardens site guide](https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/stolen-generations-marker/proposed-locations) documents nearby drinking fountains and public toilets around Boathouse Drive. Those amenities are in the wider precinct. Carry water for a long run, and use current signs to find a working refill and an open toilet.

Run the Tan reports lighting between 5 am and midnight. Choose a start time that gives you enough visibility to read the gravel surface and see other users. Lighting alone cannot establish after-dark safety. For a dark session, arrange company where useful, carry a light if needed and reassess conditions when you arrive.

The council identifies Flinders Street Station and St Kilda Road tram stops as access points for nearby Alexandra Gardens. Plan a walking connection to your chosen Tan start, or include that distance explicitly in your run. A transport connection adds distance beyond the 3.827 km circuit, so keep it separate from the lap totals.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long is one lap of The Tan?

Run the Tan publishes an official lap distance of 3.827 km. Its event course starts and finishes at the Pillars of Wisdom and runs clockwise, keeping the gardens on the right.

### How many Tan laps make 30 km?

Seven official laps total 26.789 km, leaving a calculated 3.211 km for a 30 km session. Eight laps total 30.616 km and return you to your start. GPS readings can differ from the published lap arithmetic.

### Is The Tan suitable for marathon-pace training?

It can suit effort-based blocks, but the Anderson Street climb and shared path make constant pace less useful. Ease the pace on the climb, give other users room and compare your effort across repeat laps.

### Is The Tan lit after dark?

Run the Tan reports lighting from 5 am to midnight. Lighting does not establish personal safety or guarantee that nearby toilets or garden gates are open. Check conditions and take a light if visibility requires it.
